gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the EverFrost 2's $359.99 second battery (288 Wh LFP) fits only the EverFrost 2 40L and 58L and not the first-generation EverFrost, or that the cooler only charges from solar when a battery is installed.
standout_why: I compared against GearJunkie (rank 1), Gift Sitter (rank 2) and lovethe88 wheels (rank 5). Car and Driver (rank 8) refused the fetch. GearJunkie does review the EverFrost 2 40. It gives a 299 Wh battery, while Anker says 288 Wh, and it mentions 100 W solar, 12/24 V DC and use as a power bank. It does not name the first-generation exclusion, say which coolers take the add-on battery, give its price, mention the second battery bay or say solar needs a battery installed. Gift Sitter and lovethe88 do not cover Anker or battery fit at all and list only cable types. GearJunkie's BougeRV pick is the CRD45 with a 173 Wh pack. It does not say that BougeRV's current 240 Wh pack fits only the new CRH20, CRX3, CRD2 V2.0 and Rocky V3.0.
decides: It confirms the EverFrost 2 40L as the wheeled pick with extra battery runtime. It has two battery bays, so one more maker battery doubles the onboard storage to 576 Wh. A shopper must buy the EverFrost 2 battery, not a gen-1 pack, and Anker's own bundle ($1,159.99) undercuts cooler plus battery bought apart ($799.99 + $359.99 = $1,159.98, a one-cent difference, so the price is the same). A shopper who plans to use solar only must keep a battery in the cooler. On the BougeRV side, the cheaper current route is the CRD2 V2.0 with the $189.99 240 Wh battery. The 240 Wh pack is not listed for the older CRD45 that GearJunkie picked.

The FAQ gives '100W solar panel (12-30V input)', but an MPPT note on the same page says 11–28 V, so the page contradicts itself. The 23L page has the same condition: 'Make sure at least one removable battery is attached inside the compartment when recharging it with a solar panel.'
